# IoT Fleet Provisioning Events

The `iotFleetProvisioning` event creates an AWS IoT fleet provisioning template and makes your Lambda function its [pre-provisioning hook](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/pre-provisioning-hook.html). When a device registers through fleet provisioning, AWS IoT calls the function first, and provisions the device only if the function allows it. Use it to check serial numbers or other device parameters before AWS IoT creates the device's thing, certificate and policy. The Framework creates the template; you supply the template body and an IAM provisioning role.

The following `serverless.yml` creates the template `sensor-fleet`, its provisioning role, and the `validateDevice` hook function:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-device-fleet

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  validateDevice:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iotFleetProvisioning:
          templateName: sensor-fleet
          templateBody: ${file(template.json)}
          provisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt IotProvisioningRole.Arn

resources:
  Resources:
    IotProvisioningRole:
      Type: AWS::IAM::Role
      Properties:
        AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              Principal:
                Service: iot.amazonaws.com
              Action: sts:AssumeRole
        ManagedPolicyArns:
          - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSIoTThingsRegistration
```

`template.json` sits next to `serverless.yml` and holds the provisioning template (see [Provisioning template body](#provisioning-template-body-templatebody)). A function can have only one `iotFleetProvisioning` event.

## `iotFleetProvisioning` event settings

The `iotFleetProvisioning` event takes an object with these keys:

| Key                   | Type                                     | Default                     | Description                                                          |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `templateBody`        | Object                                   | Required                    | The provisioning template document.                                  |
| `provisioningRoleArn` | String (ARN) or CloudFormation intrinsic | Required                    | The IAM role AWS IoT assumes to create the device's resources.       |
| `templateName`        | String                                   | Generated by CloudFormation | The template name. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 1 to 36 characters. |
| `enabled`             | Boolean                                  | `true`                      | Whether devices can provision with the template.                     |

## Provisioning template body (`templateBody`)

The `iotFleetProvisioning` event's `templateBody` is the [provisioning template](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/provision-template.html#fleet-provision-template) as an object; the Framework converts it to a JSON string for AWS IoT. Keep the template in a JSON file and load it with `${file(template.json)}`, which the Framework resolves to an object relative to the service directory. The following `template.json` creates a thing named after the device's serial number, activates the certificate the device created, and attaches the existing AWS IoT policy `SensorDevicePolicy`:

```json
{
  "Parameters": {
    "SerialNumber": { "Type": "String" }
  },
  "Resources": {
    "thing": {
      "Type": "AWS::IoT::Thing",
      "Properties": {
        "ThingName": {
          "Fn::Join": ["", ["sensor_", { "Ref": "SerialNumber" }]]
        }
      }
    },
    "certificate": {
      "Type": "AWS::IoT::Certificate",
      "Properties": {
        "CertificateId": { "Ref": "AWS::IoT::Certificate::Id" },
        "Status": "Active"
      }
    },
    "policy": {
      "Type": "AWS::IoT::Policy",
      "Properties": {
        "PolicyName": "SensorDevicePolicy"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`Ref` and `Fn::Join` here are AWS IoT template functions that AWS IoT evaluates for each device, not CloudFormation functions. The [fleet provisioning template example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/provision-template.html#fleet-provisioning-example) shows mappings, device configuration and an inline policy document.

## Provisioning role (`provisioningRoleArn`)

The `iotFleetProvisioning` event's `provisioningRoleArn` is the IAM role AWS IoT assumes to create things and certificates in your account. The role must trust the `iot.amazonaws.com` service principal and have the `AWSIoTThingsRegistration` managed policy, as [Provisioning by claim](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/provision-wo-cert.html#claim-based) describes. The Framework doesn't create this role:

- To create it in the same service, define it under `resources` and pass `!GetAtt <LogicalId>.Arn`, as in the first example on this page.
- To use an existing role, pass its ARN, for example `provisioningRoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/iot-provisioning-role`.

The value accepts an ARN string or the CloudFormation functions `Fn::GetAtt`, `Ref`, `Fn::ImportValue`, `Fn::Join` and `Fn::Sub`.

## Template name (`templateName`)

Devices name the template in the MQTT topics they use to register (`$aws/provisioning-templates/<templateName>/provision/<payload-format>`, where the payload format is `json` or `cbor`), and their claim certificate's AWS IoT policy allows those topics, so set the `iotFleetProvisioning` event's `templateName` to a fixed value. Without `templateName`, CloudFormation generates a name from the stack and resource names. Template names allow letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 36 characters, and are unique per account and Region; include the stage when you deploy several stages to one account:

```yaml
functions:
  validateDevice:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iotFleetProvisioning:
          templateName: sensor-fleet-${sls:stage}
          templateBody: ${file(template.json)}
          provisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt IotProvisioningRole.Arn
```

Changing `templateName` replaces the template, and devices must use the new name.

## Disable a provisioning template

To stop devices from provisioning with the template without removing it, set the `iotFleetProvisioning` event's `enabled` to `false`:

```yaml
functions:
  validateDevice:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iotFleetProvisioning:
          templateName: sensor-fleet
          templateBody: ${file(template.json)}
          provisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt IotProvisioningRole.Arn
          enabled: false
```

The template stays deployed in a disabled state. Set `enabled` back to `true`, or remove the key, and deploy again to turn it on.

## AWS resources and permissions for `iotFleetProvisioning` events

For the `iotFleetProvisioning` event, the Framework adds two resources to the stack:

- An `AWS::IoT::ProvisioningTemplate` with the logical ID `<FunctionName>IotProvisioningTemplate` (for example `ValidateDeviceIotProvisioningTemplate`), with the template body, the provisioning role, the name and the enabled state from the event. Its pre-provisioning hook targets the function, or the function's alias when the function uses `provisionedConcurrency`, [SnapStart](../guide/functions.md#snapstart) or [durable functions](../guide/functions.md#durable-functions).
- An `AWS::Lambda::Permission` with the logical ID `<FunctionName>LambdaPermissionIotProvisioningTemplate`, which lets the principal `iot.amazonaws.com` call `lambda:InvokeFunction`. The template depends on the permission, so CloudFormation creates the permission first.

The function's execution role needs no extra permissions for this event. The Framework doesn't create the provisioning role, the AWS IoT policies the template attaches, or the claim certificates devices use to connect.

## Pre-provisioning hook input and response

AWS IoT invokes the function with the device's registration request, as described in [Pre-provisioning hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/pre-provisioning-hook.html#pre-provisioning-hook-input). `parameters` holds the parameters the device sent in its `RegisterThing` request:

```json
{
  "claimCertificateId": "string",
  "certificateId": "string",
  "certificatePem": "string",
  "templateArn": "arn:aws:iot:us-east-1:123456789012:provisioningtemplate/sensor-fleet",
  "clientId": "221a6d10-9c7f-42f1-9153-e52e6fc869c1",
  "parameters": {
    "SerialNumber": "SN-000123"
  }
}
```

The function returns `allowProvisioning` and, optionally, `parameterOverrides`, whose values AWS IoT adds to the request's parameters before it evaluates the template. The following `handler.mjs` allows only serial numbers of the form `SN-` followed by six digits:

```javascript
// handler.mjs
export const handler = async (event) => {
  const serialNumber = event.parameters?.SerialNumber ?? ''

  return {
    allowProvisioning: /^SN-\d{6}$/.test(serialNumber),
    parameterOverrides: {},
  }
}
```

AWS IoT rejects the registration with `ACCESS_DENIED` when the function returns anything other than `allowProvisioning: true`, throws an error, or takes longer than 5 seconds. Keep the hook's work short and set the function's `timeout` to 5 seconds or less.
